solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Officer in A & E the writer would flee?

indicators.note: in says the writer's contraction sits between the two letters either side of the ampersand

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I, and 'I would' contracts to I'D
to flee is to decamp, to run off suddenly

explanation.surface: A hospital casualty department (A & E) seems to be such a place that the writer would run away from it.
explanation.walkthrough: A & E is the British name for a hospital emergency department; the ampersand is only a link, and 'the writer' is the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: This French-derived title names a military officer serving as a general's personal assistant.

clue.text: Pulpit constructed by a Doctor Love?

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A pulpit built by a doctor called Love.
explanation.definitionFit: An early Christian church's raised reading desk, an ancestor of the pulpit.

clue.text: Water used in setting up of revolutionary kitchen device

indicators.note: used in says the water goes inside
setting up, in a down clue, says the letters are raised to read upwards

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
rain is water falling

explanation.surface: Water was used to set up some revolutionary kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'setting up' means reading upwards; 'revolutionary' looks like an adjective but is the noun, a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack or colander where washed dishes or food drip dry.

clue.text: Health worker doctor insured to accommodate firm

indicators.note: accommodate means house, so the rearranged letters take the other word inside
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

parts.note: firm in discipline means strict

explanation.surface: A medic arranges insurance to cover a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun beside 'Health worker' but is the verb signalling the anagram, giving DINURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A community nurse visiting patients at home across a local area.

clue.text: Endless battle over Hotel Metropole's last day nursery

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Crecy was a 1346 battle of the Hundred Years' War
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The fight over the last day at a grand hotel seems endless.
explanation.walkthrough: Metropole is a common grand-hotel name; 'last' takes its E.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery where infants are minded during the working day.

clue.text: Asian ruminants more regularly seen around rivers in Wales

indicators.note: seen around says the picked letters surround the rivers
regularly picks the first and third letters, at even intervals

parts.note: the Usk and Dee are Welsh rivers

explanation.surface: Asian grazing animals are spotted more often near Welsh rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes M and R from 'more'; 'seen around' puts them round USK and DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hornless deer of Asia whose glands yield musk, cud-chewing animals.

clue.text: Figure in poll a voter rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A statistic emerging from an opinion poll in which a voter turned the canvasser away.
explanation.walkthrough: The run LAVO is concealed in 'poLL A VOter'; 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure in geometry is a shape, and an egg-like ellipse is one such shape.

clue.text: Sell brill — and freshwater fish

parts.note: to vend is to sell
brill is British slang for brilliant, and ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A fishmonger sells brill along with a river fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brill' looks like the flatfish but is slang for brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small whitefish found in a few lakes of Britain and northern Europe.

clue.text: Misguidedly play Romeo, initially neglecting satire

indicators.note: misguidedly suggests wrong direction, so the letters are rearranged
initially takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An actor plays Romeo badly, at first ignoring the satire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives N from 'neglecting'; 'Misguidedly' rearranges PLAYROMEO with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridicule through mocking writing, lampoons collectively, is a form of satire.

clue.text: Cheese a couple of sons consumed in the old club

indicators.note: consumed means eaten up, so the cheese takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
S is the abbreviation for son, so two of them make SS

explanation.surface: Two sons eat a cheese while at some old-fashioned gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a society, but this is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden golf club equivalent to a two-wood, now an obsolete name.

clue.text: Reprobate spoken of by Shakespearean corporal? It means the same thing

indicators.note: by means beside, so the corporal's name follows the sounded word
spoken of says the word for a reprobate is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a reprobate is an unprincipled person, a sinner
Corporal Nym is one of Falstaff's cronies in Shakespeare's Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.surface: A villain is described in speech by one of Shakespeare's soldiers, and the clue adds a remark about meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'sinner Nym' sounds like the answer: the first word gives its opening syllables, Nym the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the same meaning as another is described exactly by this phrase.

clue.text: Not far removed from husband in observing very little

parts.note: something not far from another is beside it

indicators.note: in puts the husband inside the word for observing

parts.note: noting means observing

explanation.surface: Someone stays close to her husband while watching almost nothing happen.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a tiny amount, as when something costs a pittance.

clue.text: Novel by a French writer reportedly unknown by party

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: UN is French for a, and a writer is an author
a do is a party
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A novel by a French author, of uncertain identity, is said to be brought out by a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something novel is new and departs from convention, just as the unconventional does.

clue.text: Back a gang in Glasgow?

parts.note: in Scots, gang is the verb to go, as heard in Glasgow

explanation.surface: Supporting a criminal gang in the Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasgow is a Scottish city, and 'gang' is the Scots verb for go; 'gang' as a crew of thugs is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Back in time, as in 'years back', means in the past.

clue.text: Clumsy workman secured by expert press chief, right away

indicators.note: secured by says the worker is held inside the other letters
away says the right letter is gone from the word

parts.note: crack means expert, as in a crack shot
ED is short for editor, a newspaper's chief
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A labourer is hired by a skilled newspaper boss, then the right is withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping R leaves CACK; the ED of the editor closes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for awkward or clumsy, originally meaning left-handed.

clue.text: Spirit extremists pinched from army HQ

indicators.note: the letters at the two extremes are stolen, leaving the inside of the word

parts.note: barracks are where an army is based

explanation.surface: Militants stole liquor from a military headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists pinched from' removes B and S, the outermost letters of BARRACKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A distilled liquor of the East, made from rice, palm sap or sugar cane.

clue.text: Terrible news Bert spread about

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Bert spreads some dreadful news around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges NEWSBERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Things scattered over a surface have been strewn about it, an old literary verb form.

clue.text: Booth, perhaps, with two hoofed mammals in

indicators.note: two says the mammal's name appears twice

parts.note: an ass is a hoofed mammal, the donkey

explanation.surface: A market stall with a pair of donkeys inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: John Wilkes Booth shot Abraham Lincoln; 'Booth' poses as a stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Booth is an example of a killer of a political leader.

clue.text: Lament retirement of old nurse originally showing enthusiasm

parts.note: to keen is to wail in mourning

indicators.note: retirement is a drawing back, so the nurse's letters go into reverse

parts.note: SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, a British nursing grade now discontinued

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone mourns the retirement of an elderly nurse while showing eagerness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement of' turns SEN to NES; 'originally' takes S from 'showing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagerness and zeal are what being keen amounts to.

clue.text: Old member overwhelmed by drink, for instance

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: overwhelmed says the member is engulfed inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A former MP was drunk, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A case cited to illustrate is what an instance is.

clue.text: Marksman quietly leaving cutter

indicators.note: leaving says the quiet letter departs from the word

parts.note: a snipper is one who snips, a cutter
P stands for piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter slips away silently from a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes P from SNIPPER; 'cutter' looks like a boat but is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden rifleman who picks off targets from cover is a marksman.

clue.text: Fuss over bishop's parsley, perhaps?

parts.note: pother is an old word for a fuss or commotion
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman fusses over his parsley.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is an example of a leafy plant grown for cooking.

clue.text: A writer enclosed one in written-up record

indicators.note: in puts the other letters inside the reversed record
written up, in a down clue, says the letters read upwards

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed on letters
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A writer encloses one item in a record kept for posterity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written-up' gives PL; 'enclosed' is the abbreviation seen at the foot of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything used for writing can be called a writer, as this graphite tool is.

clue.text: Woman using handbag every so often

indicators.note: every so often picks letters at intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: A woman occasionally carries a handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every so often' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'handbag'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female forename, as of the mathematician Lovelace.

clue.text: Property getting European in right tizzy!

indicators.note: in puts the European letter between the two words

parts.note: right as an intensifier, as in 'a right mess', means real
to be in a tizzy is to be in a state

explanation.surface: A house purchase leaves a European in a real panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a right tizzy' is British for 'in a real state', with 'right' an intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Land and buildings are property, as in the trade of buying and selling homes.

clue.text: Joint head of kindergarten born in Paris

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of the word

parts.note: nee is the French for born

explanation.surface: A nursery school headteacher was born in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge of the leg between thigh and shin is a joint.

clue.text: Bird-watchers look to them for a bob or two

definitions.text: Bird-watchers look to them for a bob or two

parts.words: Bird-watchers look to them for a bob or two
parts.note: these birds bob up and down on stream rocks, and pickpockets dip for a bob, an old shilling

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers count on certain birds for a few coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Dippers are stream birds known for bobbing; a bob is also a shilling, old British money, and a dipper is slang for a pickpocket after cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of songbirds that wade streams, famous for constant bobbing movements.

clue.text: Article on illegal activity associated with part of Ukraine

indicators.note: on says the article is placed after the other word

parts.note: crime is illegal activity
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about crime in a region of Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for the Black Sea peninsula, as in the war of the 1850s.

clue.text: Nest built by squirrel in low cart, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak says the cart's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a dray is a low flat cart, used for brewery barrels

explanation.surface: A squirrel has made its nest in a low cart, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: The twiggy home a squirrel constructs in a tree has this specific name.

clue.text: Trendy priest spread bilge, lacking qualification

parts.note: in means fashionable
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashionable cleric talks rubbish without the right credentials.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the crossword's favourite priest; 'spread' rearranges BILGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not entitled or qualified to take part is disqualified, unfit to be chosen.
